question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European conflicts and contested settlements]
options: Swally Hole (Surat) — Naval battle site where the English fleet under Captain Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese in 1612
Pulicat — Coromandel base where the Dutch built Fort Geldria in 1613 to challenge Portuguese dominance in the textile trade
Chinsurah — Bengal base established by the Dutch in 1656, which eclipsed Portuguese trade in the Hugli region
Diu — Strategic island fortress captured by the English East India Company in 1622 to control trade in the Gulf of Cambay
wrong_fact: Diu was never captured by the English East India Company. It remained under Portuguese control continuously from 1535 until 1961.
explanation: Diu remained a Portuguese possession until India annexed it in 1661 (along with Goa and Daman). The English never captured it. Swally Hole, Pulicat (Fort Geldria), and Chinsurah are all correctly matched with their respective European rivalries and settlements.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Strategic outposts lost to European competitors]
options: Ormuz — Key Persian Gulf checkpoint captured from the Portuguese in 1622 by a joint Anglo-Persian force
Malacca — Strategic Southeast Asian strait port captured by the Dutch in 1641 after a devastating five-month siege
Cochin — Portuguese Malabar headquarters captured by the Dutch in 1663, ending Portuguese monopoly in the pepper trade
Daman — Northern enclave captured by the French East India Company in 1668 to establish their primary base in India
wrong_fact: Daman was never captured by the French. It remained under Portuguese control until 1961. The French established their first factory in Surat in 1668.
explanation: Daman remained a Portuguese territory and was never taken by the French. The French established their presence in India starting at Surat (1668) and later Pondicherry. Ormuz was lost to a joint Safavid-English force in 1622, Malacca fell to the Dutch in 1641, and Cochin was captured by the Dutch in 1663.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European naval blockades and regional power shifts]
options: Colombo — Ceylon stronghold captured by the Dutch in 1656, stripping the Portuguese of their primary source of cinnamon
Nagapattinam — Coromandel port captured by the Dutch in 1658, ending Portuguese influence on the southern east coast of India
Quilon — Malabar fort captured by the Dutch in 1661 as part of their campaign to expel the Portuguese from the pepper-growing region
Goa — Capital city whose outer harbor was blockaded continuously by the English Royal Navy from 1639 to 1644
wrong_fact: The naval blockade of Goa between 1639 and 1644 was conducted by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) fleet, not the English Royal Navy.
explanation: During the Dutch-Portuguese War, the Dutch VOC fleet blockaded Goa repeatedly (especially from 1639 to 1644) to disrupt Portuguese trade and prevent reinforcement ships from Lisbon. The English were not blockading Goa and had signed a truce with the Portuguese in India in 1635 (Methuen-like local agreement by President Methwold). Colombo, Nagapattinam, and Quilon are correct Dutch conquests.
